sentences.text: Metopacanthus was an extinct genus of holocephalan cartilaginous fish that lived in Europe during the Early Jurassic epoch.
This animal possessed an unusual jaw-like structure located over its skull.
It also had a long fin spine measuring 33 cm in length.
The genus Metopacanthus was first described by Zittel in 1887.
Metopacanthus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the family Myriacanthidae.
Metopacanthus granulatus is the type species of the genus Metopacanthus.
The species lived between the Sinemurian and Toarcian stages, from 199.5 to 182.9 million years ago.
Fossils of Metopacanthus are found in the Toarcian stage of the Posidonia Shale in Germany.
